 Lao PDR Holds 23rd National Monsoon Forum to Strengthen Weather Forecasting and Early Warning Systems
 11/11/2026 13:05 
 Email 
 Print 
 329 
 KPL 
 The 23rd Lao PDR National Monsoon Forum for the Northeast Monsoon Season opened in Vientiane on November 10, 2026, bringing together government agencies, international organisations and development partners to review weather forecasting performance and strengthen early warning systems. 
 (KPL)  The forum was chaired by Director General of the Department of Meteorology and Hydrology (DMH) Vilana Sonnasinh and attended by Peter Khillil Ferrer, a representative of the Regional Integrated Multi-Hazard Early Warning System (RIMES), along with representatives from international organisations, development partners and relevant government agencies. 
 In his opening remarks, Vilana stressed the importance of reviewing the performance of weather and hydrological forecasts during the 2026 rainy season, particularly their accuracy and reliability in reflecting actual weather and water conditions. 
 The forum will also assess how government agencies and other sectors have used forecasts and early warnings in planning, decision-making and preparing for climate-related risks. 
 He called on participants to share practical feedback, identify operational challenges and recommend ways to improve the accuracy, timeliness and accessibility of forecast information so it better meets the needs of different sectors. 
 Vilana also encouraged open and constructive discussions, urging participants to highlight real challenges and propose practical solutions that can be implemented. 
 He expressed confidence that stronger cooperation and coordination among government agencies and development partners would improve forecasting services, strengthen early warning capabilities and promote the effective use of climate information. 
 These efforts are expected to help reduce disaster risks and their impact on communities, protect people's livelihoods and support sustainable socio-economic development across Laos.
